item.title: Radiocarpal AP / PA Glide
clinicalUse: Painful restriction where accessory glide changes the comparable sign
patientPosition: Sitting with forearm fully supported on table and hand over edge.
therapistPosition: Sit facing the hand so the wrist joint line is easy to control.
stabilization: Stabilize distal radius/ulna firmly but comfortably.
contact: Mobilizing hand contacts proximal carpal row broadly, avoiding excessive pressure over superficial nerves/tendons.
forceDirection: Apply AP or PA glide according to the restricted movement and response.
Use low grade for pain and higher grade for stiffness when safe.
steps: 6. Follow with active ROM and grip/loading.
mistakes: Moving whole forearm instead of carpus.
Aggressive mobilization after recent fracture without clearance.
safety: Avoid acute fracture, unstable carpal injury, inflammatory flare or unhealed surgery.
item.visualCue: Distal forearm fixed → proximal carpal row glides AP/PA → re-test wrist ROM.

subTechniques.name: Radiocarpal Dorsal Glide for Wrist Flexion
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve wrist flexion when dorsal carpal glide is restricted.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with forearm supported and wrist just off the table.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the distal radius/ulna and grasp the proximal carpal row broadly.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the carpals dorsally while the forearm remains stable.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Keep the force at the radiocarpal joint rather than pulling the whole hand.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute carpal instability or fracture.

subTechniques.name: Radiocarpal Volar Glide for Wrist Extension
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve wrist extension when volar carpal glide is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with forearm supported and wrist accessible.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize distal radius/ulna and contact the proximal carpal row.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the carpal row volarly relative to the radius.
subTechniques.reassess: Wrist extension and weight-bearing through the hand.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Re-test a meaningful task such as push-up position or getting up from a chair if that was the original limitation.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Respect ligament injury and postoperative precautions.
